note: ER+ MCF-7 xenografts sent cixutumumab and dalotuzumab into breast cancer, where every randomised trial was null; only the models that found no effect (IGF1R-lost tamoxifen-resistant cells, aromatase xenografts) matched the clinic, and FDA says monkeys missed the class's hyperglycaemia.
label: Breast cancer (anti-IGF1R)

engagement.model: ER+ MCF-7 breast xenografts in nude mice (IMC-A12, h7C10)
engagement.note: IMC-A12 blocked IGF-I-driven MAPK/Akt signalling and drove IGF-IR internalisation and degradation in MCF7 cells; in vivo blockade read as tumour growth. Opens the dalotuzumab track by proxy: the model's first use was IMC-A12 (cixutumumab); dalotuzumab's own h7C10 followed in MCF-7 xenografts in 2004 (Goetsch).
engagement.short: IGF-IR degraded and Akt blocked in MCF7
engagement.quote: In xenograft tumor models in vivo, IGF-IR blockade by A12 was shown to occur rapidly, resulting in significant growth inhibition of breast, renal, and pancreatic tumors.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Burtrum 2003 has no DOI; PubMed record cited). Goetsch 2005 (doi 10.1002/ijc.20543) put dalotuzumab's parent h7C10 in the same MCF-7 xenograft, so both members' parents sit on this track.

engagement.model: ER+ MCF-7 breast xenografts in nude mice (IMC-A12, h7C10)
engagement.note: Dalotuzumab phase 1: paired tumour biopsies showed loss of IGF-1R, downstream signalling and Ki67 at the doses later used in breast trials. Patients were mixed solid tumours, not breast cancer, coded other_disease.
engagement.short: Tumour IGF-1R and signalling fell in patients
engagement.quote: Decreases in tumor IGF-1R, downstream receptor signaling, and Ki67 expression were observed.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Mixed solid tumours, admitted on the engagement rule that non-disease subjects count. Breast-specific support: Ma 2013 (doi 10.1007/s10549-013-2528-8) serum IGF-1 rise with cixutumumab in MBC; NCT00759785 (results 2017-04-14) growth-factor-signature fall in 28.6% of ER+ and 17.6% of TN tumours after one 20 mg/kg dose.
engagement.magnitude_basis: receptor loss and pathway inhibition, qualitative in both
engagement.population: IGF-1R-expressing advanced solid tumours (mixed, not breast-only)
engagement.judgement: The model's PD readout (IGF-1R downregulation, Akt/MAPK blockade) was measured in dosed patients and moved the same way, so same. The breast-only registry readout (NCT00759785) moved in only a minority, which is why magnitude is direction_only and the status is not strengthened.
engagement.reason: Receptor loss reproduced in patient tumours

engagement.model: Tamoxifen-resistant MCF-7L cells and tamoxifen-treated xenografts (dalotuzumab)
engagement.note: Model readout is loss of IGF1R in tamoxifen-treated tumours; Gradishar 2016 measured tumour IGF-1R as a predictive biomarker, not as a PD readout in dosed patients.
engagement.short: IGF1R loss not read in dosed patients
engagement.quote: We conclude that cells selected for tamoxifen resistance in vitro have downregulated IGF1R making antibodies directed against this receptor ineffective.
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC4520534). In-vitro TamR cells plus tamoxifen-treated MCF-7L xenografts; dalotuzumab is the antibody used.
engagement.judgement: No patient series paired tamoxifen-resistant tumour IGF1R levels with antibody dosing, so untested rather than an empty cell.

engagement.model: MCF7 cells in vitro and NSCLC patient-derived xenograft LXFA629 (ridaforolimus plus dalotuzumab)
engagement.note: Readout was enhanced pathway inhibition with the combination; the phase 1 in the same paper reports DLTs and responses, no PD in the abstract.
engagement.short: Combination pathway PD not reported in patients
engagement.quote: Preclinical studies demonstrated enhanced pathway inhibition with ridaforolimus and dalotuzumab.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the models are not named in the abstract. Preclinical work and the phase 1 (NCT00730379, started 2008-07) are in one paper published 2014-10-15, so the model data were public only after the phase 1 and possibly after NCT01234857 read out.
engagement.judgement: Abstract gives no patient PD measure for the combination; untested.

engagement.model: MCF-7/AC-1 aromatase-expressing xenografts under letrozole (dalotuzumab, ridaforolimus)
engagement.note: RNAseq showed dalotuzumab alone downregulated IGF/insulin signalling in xenografts; no patient transcriptional pairing was published for this model.
engagement.quote: With the exception of MK-0646, all single agent and combination treatment arms effectively inhibited xenograft tumor growth, albeit to varying degrees.
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5073873). Mayo/Merck collaboration; the paper cites completed dalotuzumab-ridaforolimus trials, so the model was run while the clinic was already reading out.
engagement.judgement: NCT00759785's growth-factor signature is a different signature in a different design and is credited to track A, not here.

engagement.model: Merck 101-gene growth-factor pathway signature (GFS) scored on patient tumour biopsies (dalotuzumab)
engagement.population: ER-positive luminal B and triple-negative breast cancer, presurgical single dose of dalotuzumab 20 mg/kg
engagement.confidence_note: Registry record only (first posted 2008-09-25). The 101-gene GFS is Merck's growth-factor-pathway signature (US patent 8392127, Watters/Loboda/Nebozhyn: found in AKT-inhibitor-phenotyped colon lines, checked against growth-factor-stimulated MCF7/HT29 and MK-0646 xenograft growth inhibition); a patent is not an admissible tier, so the model side rests on the registry. It is not the Creighton 2008 MCF-7 IGF-I signature.
engagement.note: Merck's 101-gene growth-factor pathway signature, scored on paired tumour biopsies, set as the proof-of-biology endpoint: dalotuzumab should lower it in at least 40% of patients.
engagement.quote: The primary hypothesis is that dalotuzumab will induce a decrease in the GFS in at least 40% of participants.
engagement.judgement: A separate system from the MCF-7 xenograft tracks: an in-silico transcriptional classifier applied to patient biopsies, carrying its own prediction (signature reversal in at least 40% of dosed tumours).

engagement.model: Merck 101-gene growth-factor pathway signature (GFS) scored on patient tumour biopsies (dalotuzumab)
engagement.population: ER-positive luminal B and triple-negative breast cancer, presurgical single dose of dalotuzumab 20 mg/kg
engagement.magnitude_basis: share of dosed tumours whose GFS fell (28.6% ER+, 17.6% TN) against the sponsor hypothesis of at least 40%
engagement.confidence_note: Registry results only (posted 2017-04-14; results first submitted 2016-11-21; no peer-reviewed report found). Values are percentages with 80% CI (as posted); the ER+ interval (13.1-49.2) spans 40% even at that width, so the miss is at point-estimate level, and a reader applying 'partial' would score same. The direct secondary readout, IGF1R membrane H-score, fell by a median 104.5 in ER+ and 11.5 in TN (n=13 each), so the receptor was hit while the signature mostly did not move. The model side is the same registry record (the signature's derivation is only in a patent).
engagement.note: Ruling: the 40% bar is the sponsor's trial hypothesis, not a number the signature stated, so it is not the prediction. The signature fell in 28.6% of ER+ and 17.6% of TN tumours: direction held.
engagement.short: GFS fell in fewer than 40% predicted
engagement.quote: Percentage of Participants Demonstrating a Decrease in the Growth Factor Signature (GFS): ER-positive Luminal B 28.6 (13.1 to 49.2); Triple Negative 17.6 (6.7 to 35.2) percentage of participants.
engagement.judgement: Rule question settled under the brief (a sponsor's target is not the model's): engagement asks whether the readout moved in dosed humans; it moved, in a minority, so same with direction_only and low confidence. The registry makes no call.
engagement.reason: Signature fell, in a minority of tumours

dose.model: ER+ MCF-7 breast xenografts in nude mice (IMC-A12, h7C10)
dose.note: Mice were dosed to tumour growth inhibition; no human exposure target is stated in the abstract.
dose.short: No exposure target in the abstract
dose.quote: In xenograft tumor models in vivo, IGF-IR blockade by A12 was shown to occur rapidly, resulting in significant growth inhibition of breast, renal, and pancreatic tumors.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Burtrum 2003 has no DOI; PubMed record cited). Goetsch 2005 (doi 10.1002/ijc.20543) put dalotuzumab's parent h7C10 in the same MCF-7 xenograft, so both members' parents sit on this track.

dose.model: Tamoxifen-resistant MCF-7L cells and tamoxifen-treated xenografts (dalotuzumab)
dose.note: In-vitro resistance model with no exposure target; it predicted inactivity regardless of dose.
dose.short: Model predicts inactivity, no dose target
dose.quote: We conclude that cells selected for tamoxifen resistance in vitro have downregulated IGF1R making antibodies directed against this receptor ineffective.
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC4520534). In-vitro TamR cells plus tamoxifen-treated MCF-7L xenografts; dalotuzumab is the antibody used.
dose.judgement: A model that predicts no response has no exposure target to reach; dose cannot be scored on this track.

dose.model: MCF7 cells in vitro and NSCLC patient-derived xenograft LXFA629 (ridaforolimus plus dalotuzumab)
dose.note: No exposure target stated; the phase 1 hit mTOR DLTs at ridaforolimus doses lower than expected and the triple-therapy arm later ran ridaforolimus at 10 mg.
dose.short: Partner dose cut by toxicity, no margin
dose.quote: Preclinical studies demonstrated enhanced pathway inhibition with ridaforolimus and dalotuzumab.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the models are not named in the abstract. Preclinical work and the phase 1 (NCT00730379, started 2008-07) are in one paper published 2014-10-15, so the model data were public only after the phase 1 and possibly after NCT01234857 read out.
dose.judgement: Decision 16: ridaforolimus's effective dose was not deliverable with dalotuzumab (stomatitis), but no tolerability margin was stated by the model, so the row is 'no stated margin: untested'. Dalotuzumab's own 10 mg/kg weekly was reached.

dose.model: MCF-7/AC-1 aromatase-expressing xenografts under letrozole (dalotuzumab, ridaforolimus)
dose.note: Mice were dosed to a 28-day endpoint with no plasma exposure or tolerability target stated.
dose.quote: With the exception of MK-0646, all single agent and combination treatment arms effectively inhibited xenograft tumor growth, albeit to varying degrees.
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5073873). Mayo/Merck collaboration; the paper cites completed dalotuzumab-ridaforolimus trials, so the model was run while the clinic was already reading out.
dose.judgement: No target to compare with Rugo 2017's 10 mg/kg weekly; untested.

efficacy.model: ER+ MCF-7 breast xenografts in nude mice (IMC-A12, h7C10)
efficacy.note: Single-agent IMC-A12 and h7C10 significantly inhibited ER+ MCF-7 xenograft growth, the class's pitch for breast cancer.
efficacy.short: MCF-7 xenografts inhibited by single agent
efficacy.quote: In xenograft tumor models in vivo, IGF-IR blockade by A12 was shown to occur rapidly, resulting in significant growth inhibition of breast, renal, and pancreatic tumors.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Burtrum 2003 has no DOI; PubMed record cited). Goetsch 2005 (doi 10.1002/ijc.20543) put dalotuzumab's parent h7C10 in the same MCF-7 xenograft, so both members' parents sit on this track.

efficacy.model: ER+ MCF-7 breast xenografts in nude mice (IMC-A12, h7C10)
efficacy.note: Randomised phase 2: adding cixutumumab to capecitabine plus lapatinib in trastuzumab-pretreated HER2+ breast cancer did not improve PFS (HR 1.04). Design: combination trial (cixutumumab added to capecitabine plus lapatinib), scored on its PFS primary endpoint; partner named in combination_with.
efficacy.quote: Progression-free Survival (PFS): Arm A 6.0 months (4.3 to 8.6), Arm B 4.9 months (2.9 to 8.5); Hazard Ratio (HR) 1.04 (0.58 to 1.89), p = .89.
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results record (tier 3; posting date typed 'estimated' on the record). Quote is the record's primary-outcome table, not prose. No peer-reviewed paper located for this NCI trial.
efficacy.judgement: Earliest public member datum in breast cancer, so it sets the year (rule 6). The HER2+ add-on design is a weaker test of an ER+ xenograft than Gradishar's, hence medium confidence and the strengthening entry below.

efficacy.model: ER+ MCF-7 breast xenografts in nude mice (IMC-A12, h7C10)
efficacy.note: Randomised phase 2 in HR+ breast cancer progressed on antiestrogen: median PFS 2.0 and 3.1 months, no efficacy; dalotuzumab later failed twice (HR 1.00, 1.18). Design: two cixutumumab arms (alone, or with the antiestrogen patients had progressed on), no untreated control; scored on the PFS primary as the authors call it. Dalotuzumab now has its own track below.
efficacy.short: No efficacy in HR+ breast cancer
efficacy.quote: Cixutumumab (10 mg/kg) with or without antiestrogen q2w had an acceptable safety profile, but no significant clinical efficacy.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Epub 2015-08-31; NCT00728949 results posted 2018-06-06. No untreated control arm (cixutumumab +/- antiestrogen), so the null rests on the PFS bar and the authors' conclusion.
efficacy.judgement: Class-level prediction (anti-IGF1R antibody inhibits ER+ breast tumour growth) contradicted by every member tested: cixutumumab (two randomised phase 2s, one single-arm phase 2 with 0% ORR), dalotuzumab (two randomised phase 2s), and teprotumumab/R1507 whose breast phase 2 (NCT00796107) stopped at 6 patients with no reported efficacy. Veligrotug has no breast cancer trial; it is untested, not a failure.

patient_trials.quote: Tumor Response Rate (TRR): Phase II 0 (95% CI 0 to 13.3) percentage of patients with response.
The combination of ridaforolimus plus dalotuzumab was no more effective than exemestane in patients with advanced ER-positive breast cancer, and the incidence of adverse events was higher.
R/D/E did not improve PFS compared with R/E.
Due to the discontinuation of compound development, this study has been terminated.

efficacy.reason: Every member failed in breast patients

efficacy.model: Tamoxifen-resistant MCF-7L cells and tamoxifen-treated xenografts (dalotuzumab)
efficacy.note: Built after early trials had shown no benefit of IGF1R inhibitors added to endocrine therapy: TamR cells lose IGF1R and dalotuzumab has no effect on them.
efficacy.short: TamR cells lose IGF1R, antibody inert
efficacy.quote: We conclude that cells selected for tamoxifen resistance in vitro have downregulated IGF1R making antibodies directed against this receptor ineffective.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC4520534). In-vitro TamR cells plus tamoxifen-treated MCF-7L xenografts; dalotuzumab is the antibody used.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the same paper is scored as a retrodiction below.

efficacy.model: Tamoxifen-resistant MCF-7L cells and tamoxifen-treated xenografts (dalotuzumab)
efficacy.note: Paper states the clinical null and reproduces it: dalotuzumab inert in TamR cells and adds nothing to tamoxifen in xenografts, because IGF1R is lost. Ruling: for efficacy any drug's earlier patient result for the same target and action makes a model a retrodiction, so the earlier ganitumab null (not a tile member) keeps this retro; drug is dalotuzumab, the antibody the model was run with.
efficacy.short: Model reproduces the known endocrine-resistant null
efficacy.quote: The majority of anti-IGF1R clinical trials are in estrogen receptor-positive patients who have progressed on prior endocrine therapy; early reports show no benefit for addition of IGF1R inhibitors to endocrine therapy in this setting.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. The 'early reports' are not identified by drug in the abstract; the member trials (NCT00728949, NCT01234857) had not published by May 2012, so which class data the authors knew is unverified.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: no added benefit in model and in early trials, qualitative
efficacy.judgement: Rule question settled by the 2026-11-09 retrodiction ruling: engagement and efficacy count a prior patient result from any drug of the same target and action, so the ganitumab plus endocrine-therapy null that Fagan cites makes the model a retrodiction; it reproduced the null, so retro.

efficacy.model: Tamoxifen-resistant MCF-7L cells and tamoxifen-treated xenografts (dalotuzumab)
efficacy.note: First member result public after the model: cixutumumab in HR+ patients progressed on antiestrogen showed no efficacy, as the IGF1R-loss model predicted. Cixutumumab was never run in this model; its track here is a pairing, product_in_model false, and has no separate opener.
efficacy.quote: Cixutumumab (10 mg/kg) with or without antiestrogen q2w had an acceptable safety profile, but no significant clinical efficacy.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The trial enrolled 2008-2011 but its result was first public 2015-08-31 (no earlier registry posting), so relative to the May 2012 model it is a fresh prediction unless a conference abstract preceded it; not checked. Cixutumumab, not dalotuzumab, so product_in_model false and not neg.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: no benefit predicted, none seen; PFS 2.0 and 3.1 months
efficacy.population: HR+, progressed on antiestrogen therapy (AI or tamoxifen)
efficacy.judgement: The model's negative prediction for endocrine-resistant patients agreed in direction; the trial mixed AI- and tamoxifen-progressed patients while the model is tamoxifen-specific, so direction_only and medium confidence.

efficacy.model: Tamoxifen-resistant MCF-7L cells and tamoxifen-treated xenografts (dalotuzumab)
efficacy.note: Dalotuzumab, the antibody that was inert in the TamR model, added nothing to ridaforolimus plus exemestane in NSAI-progressed ER+ patients. Design: combination trial (dalotuzumab added to ridaforolimus plus exemestane, R/D/E vs R/E), scored on its PFS primary endpoint.
efficacy.short: Dalotuzumab itself fails, as its model data showed
efficacy.quote: Median PFS was 23.3 weeks for R/D/E versus 31.9 weeks for R/E (hazard ratio 1.18; 80% CI 0.81-1.72; P = 0.565).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Trial started 2012-07, after the model's May 2012 publication. Model resistance was to tamoxifen; the trial's was to a NSAI, so the match is by mechanism (IGF1R loss) rather than by regimen.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: no added benefit in model (xenograft) and trial (PFS HR 1.18)
efficacy.population: ER+, Ki67 >=15%, progressed after a NSAI
efficacy.judgement: Decision 13 neg: the model's own data for a member fell below the class bar and that member failed in patients, judged on the data (no added benefit) rather than on the authors' framing.
efficacy.effect_size: dalotuzumab: no inhibition of proliferation or Akt phosphorylation in TamR cells; in vivo 'dalotuzumab did not enhance the effect of tamoxifen' (Fagan 2012)
efficacy.class_threshold: inhibition of IGF-I-driven growth, which dalotuzumab achieved in parental MCF-7L cells and estrogen-treated xenografts in the same paper

patient_trials.quote: Median PFS was 21.4 weeks for ridaforolimus 30 mg qd × 5 days/week plus dalotuzumab 10 mg/kg (n = 29) and 24.3 weeks for exemestane (n = 33; hazard ratio = 1.00; P = 0.5).

efficacy.reason: Model's own null for dalotuzumab held

efficacy.model: MCF7 cells in vitro and NSCLC patient-derived xenograft LXFA629 (ridaforolimus plus dalotuzumab)
efficacy.note: Ruling: the model was first public (Di Cosimo, Oct 2014) after the ridaforolimus plus dalotuzumab vs exemestane null was shown at SABCS Dec 2013, so it is a retrodiction; it predicted enhanced activity and failed to reproduce the null: contra. Design: combination, partner ridaforolimus.
efficacy.short: Model public after the R+D null it missed
efficacy.quote: The combination of ridaforolimus plus dalotuzumab was no more effective than exemestane in patients with advanced ER-positive breast cancer, and the incidence of adverse events was higher.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the models are not named in the abstract. Preclinical work and the phase 1 (NCT00730379, started 2008-07) are in one paper published 2014-10-15, so the model data were public only after the phase 1 and possibly after NCT01234857 read out.
efficacy.population: ER+ advanced breast cancer previously treated with a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction by post-dating (brief): model public 2014-10-15, member patient result public 2013-12 (SABCS, stated in Baselga 2017). Failed to reproduce it, so contra with retrodiction true; the Rugo trial below is the next test.

efficacy.model: MCF7 cells in vitro and NSCLC patient-derived xenograft LXFA629 (ridaforolimus plus dalotuzumab)
efficacy.note: Randomised phase 2 isolating dalotuzumab's contribution: adding it to ridaforolimus plus exemestane did not improve PFS (HR 1.18); R+D also failed to beat exemestane (HR 1.00). Design: combination trial (dalotuzumab added to ridaforolimus plus exemestane, R/D/E vs R/E), scored on its PFS primary endpoint. Second contra on this track: the first prospective test after the retrodiction.
efficacy.short: Adding dalotuzumab to mTOR blockade did nothing
efficacy.quote: R/D/E did not improve PFS compared with R/E.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Baselga 2017 (NCT01234857, epub 2017-03-21, no registry results) is the earlier 2017 record and is listed under patient_trials; Rugo 2017 is used because its design tests the model's claim directly. Whether the Di Cosimo preclinical data predate the NCT01234857 readout is unverified.
efficacy.population: ER+, Ki67 >=15%, progressed after a NSAI
efficacy.judgement: Separate track from D (different model, different prediction): this model predicted that adding anti-IGF1R to mTOR inhibition enhances efficacy; both randomised phase 2s said no. Rugo's authors offer the lowered ridaforolimus dose as a confounder; that is scored in dose, not here.

patient_trials.quote: The combination of ridaforolimus plus dalotuzumab was no more effective than exemestane in patients with advanced ER-positive breast cancer, and the incidence of adverse events was higher.

Six confirmed partial responses were reported (3 patients with breast cancer); 10 of 23 patients with breast cancer and 6 of 11 patients with ER(+)/high-proliferative breast cancer showed antitumor activity.

efficacy.reason: Feedback-blockade prediction failed in two trials

efficacy.model: MCF-7/AC-1 aromatase-expressing xenografts under letrozole (dalotuzumab, ridaforolimus)
efficacy.note: Dalotuzumab alone did not inhibit MCF-7/AC-1 xenografts and did not add to letrozole or to letrozole plus ridaforolimus; the authors still pitched triple therapy. Ruling: first public after the dalotuzumab null was shown (SABCS 2013), so a retrodiction that reproduced it: retro.
efficacy.quote: Data herein demonstrate that, similar to clinical trials, IGF-1R inhibition (via MK-0646) does not enhance hormonal therapy in ER-positive breast cancer cells, the results of which are may be attributable to compensatory IGF-2/IRA activity.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5073873). Mayo/Merck collaboration; the paper cites completed dalotuzumab-ridaforolimus trials, so the model was run while the clinic was already reading out.
efficacy.judgement: Ruling (retrodiction by post-dating): Becker was received 2015-06-29 and published 2016-10-20, after the member result (ridaforolimus plus dalotuzumab vs exemestane, SABCS Dec 2013); it states the clinical null and reproduces it, so retro, as the check adjudicated.

efficacy.model: MCF-7/AC-1 aromatase-expressing xenografts under letrozole (dalotuzumab, ridaforolimus)
efficacy.note: The triple regimen the model proposed was tested: dalotuzumab added to ridaforolimus plus exemestane gave no PFS gain (HR 1.18), as the xenograft data had shown. Design: combination trial (dalotuzumab added to ridaforolimus plus exemestane, R/D/E vs R/E), scored on its PFS primary endpoint. Under the ruling Rugo was first public (2017-07) after this model, so absent an earlier congress abstract it is a prospective test; the check adjudicated retro.
efficacy.short: Xenograft null for dalotuzumab held in patients
efficacy.quote: R/D/E did not improve PFS compared with R/E.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Rugo; full text for Becker. The trial completed before the model paper (2016-10-20) but its result was first public 2017-07-05 (registry 2019-03-25); if a conference abstract preceded October 2016 this becomes a retrodiction. Not checked.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: no significant added effect of dalotuzumab in model or trial
efficacy.population: ER+, Ki67 >=15%, progressed after a NSAI
efficacy.judgement: Decision 13: judged on what the data showed (dalotuzumab inert, triple not significantly better than double), not on the sponsor's 'preclinical rationalization' for triple therapy. Read on the pitch it would be contra; the data make it neg.
efficacy.effect_size: MK-0646 alone: no significant tumour growth inhibition; LET + MK-0646 similar to LET alone; triple not significant vs LET + MK-8669 (62.7% regression vs control, Becker 2016)
efficacy.class_threshold: significant tumour growth inhibition vs control, met by every other arm in the same experiment and by MCF-7 xenografts in Burtrum 2003 and Goetsch 2005
efficacy.reason: Model data, not its pitch, matched the trial

efficacy.model: Merck 101-gene growth-factor pathway signature (GFS) scored on patient tumour biopsies (dalotuzumab)
efficacy.population: ER-positive luminal B and triple-negative breast cancer, presurgical single dose of dalotuzumab 20 mg/kg
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry record only. The patent claims the GFS classifies growth-factor-deregulated tumours and predicts response, but no breast trial of a member antibody stratified or analysed outcome by GFS: NCT00759785 correlated GFS response only with IGF1R IHC, and NCT01220570 (GFS as an intermediate biomarker of response; ridaforolimus, dalotuzumab or both; 63 patients, completed 2012-12) never posted results.
efficacy.note: Signature claimed to classify growth-factor-deregulated tumours and predict response; never used to select patients for a member antibody, and NCT01220570 posted no results.
efficacy.quote: A study to evaluate the response of growth factor signatures (GFS) to a single dose of dalotuzumab in participants with triple negative (TN) or estrogen receptor (ER)-positive luminal B breast cancer.
efficacy.judgement: The response-prediction claim is a patient-level efficacy prediction, but the only comparisons made were pharmacodynamic (engagement), so efficacy stays untested on this track.

efficacy.model: ER+ MCF-7 breast xenografts in nude mice (IMC-A12, h7C10)
efficacy.note: Opens the dalotuzumab track: h7C10 (dalotuzumab) significantly inhibited MCF-7 xenograft growth. Split from efficacy 3.
efficacy.quote: Treatment of nude mice bearing either human breast cancer cells (MCF-7) or non small lung cancer cells (A549) with h7C10, or its murine parental form 7C10, inhibited significantly tumor growth.
efficacy.judgement: Track split: the same MCF-7 xenograft, run with dalotuzumab.

efficacy.model: ER+ MCF-7 breast xenografts in nude mice (IMC-A12, h7C10)
efficacy.note: Design: combination trial (dalotuzumab with ridaforolimus vs exemestane), scored on its PFS primary: HR 1.00, no benefit. First shown at SABCS December 2013. Split from efficacy 3.
efficacy.short: Dalotuzumab combination no better than exemestane
efficacy.quote: The combination of ridaforolimus plus dalotuzumab was no more effective than exemestane in patients with advanced ER-positive breast cancer, and the incidence of adverse events was higher.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for results; full text (PMC5448790) states the study was presented at SABCS 2013 (December 10-14), which dates the entry. NCT01234857 has no posted registry results.
efficacy.population: ER+ advanced breast cancer previously treated with a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor
efficacy.judgement: Track split from the cixutumumab entries: dalotuzumab, the model's own h7C10, was scored on its own randomised trial. A combination design, scored on its primary endpoint under the ruling.

patient_trials.quote: R/D/E did not improve PFS compared with R/E.

safety.model: ER+ MCF-7 breast xenografts in nude mice (IMC-A12, h7C10)
safety.note: Mouse xenografts made no tolerability statement; whether IMC-A12 or h7C10 bind mouse IGF-IR is unverified, so silence on hyperglycaemia is not scored.
safety.quote: In xenograft tumor models in vivo, IGF-IR blockade by A12 was shown to occur rapidly, resulting in significant growth inhibition of breast, renal, and pancreatic tumors.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Burtrum 2003 has no DOI; PubMed record cited). Goetsch 2005 (doi 10.1002/ijc.20543) put dalotuzumab's parent h7C10 in the same MCF-7 xenograft, so both members' parents sit on this track.
safety.judgement: Hyperglycaemia is the class's on-target harm (19% in Atzori 2011, >=10% in Higano 2015). It is scored against the mouse only if the antibody engages mouse IGF-IR, which I could not confirm at abstract level; left untested and flagged.

safety.model: Tamoxifen-resistant MCF-7L cells and tamoxifen-treated xenografts (dalotuzumab)
safety.note: Resistance model with no tolerability content.
safety.quote: We conclude that cells selected for tamoxifen resistance in vitro have downregulated IGF1R making antibodies directed against this receptor ineffective.
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC4520534). In-vitro TamR cells plus tamoxifen-treated MCF-7L xenografts; dalotuzumab is the antibody used.

safety.model: MCF7 cells in vitro and NSCLC patient-derived xenograft LXFA629 (ridaforolimus plus dalotuzumab)
safety.note: Model abstract carries no tolerability statement; the phase 1's unexpected mTOR DLTs are a clinical observation, not a model prediction.
safety.short: Combination toxicity not predicted by model
safety.quote: Preclinical studies demonstrated enhanced pathway inhibition with ridaforolimus and dalotuzumab.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the models are not named in the abstract. Preclinical work and the phase 1 (NCT00730379, started 2008-07) are in one paper published 2014-10-15, so the model data were public only after the phase 1 and possibly after NCT01234857 read out.
safety.judgement: The stomatitis at lower-than-expected ridaforolimus doses is scored in dose (no stated margin), not here.

safety.model: MCF-7/AC-1 aromatase-expressing xenografts under letrozole (dalotuzumab, ridaforolimus)
safety.note: Becker states all agents, alone and in combination, were well tolerated by body weight (data not shown); that passing claim is scored in the appended entry.
safety.quote: With the exception of MK-0646, all single agent and combination treatment arms effectively inhibited xenograft tumor growth, albeit to varying degrees.
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5073873). Mayo/Merck collaboration; the paper cites completed dalotuzumab-ridaforolimus trials, so the model was run while the clinic was already reading out.
safety.judgement: Opening entry. The passing tolerability claim is a safety prediction under the ruling and is scored below against the dalotuzumab plus ridaforolimus patients.

safety.note: Ruling: breast cancer patients were measured on teprotumumab (NCT00796107, 1/6 hyperglycaemia), so they set the status, not the imported TED data. FDA: 'The monkey toxicology studies did not predict these effects.'
safety.short: Monkeys silent; breast patients had hyperglycaemia
safety.quote: Hyperglycaemia: R1507 in Combination With Letrozole, 1/6 participants affected (2 events).
safety.confidence_note: Registry results table (tier 3; posted 2020-11-13; 6 patients, terminated). Model side: FDA PharmR 761143, whose reviewer states the monkey studies did not predict hyperglycaemia (10% vs 1% in TED). TED hyperglycaemia public 2017 (Smith, NEJM) recalled, not re-read. Monkey study years not given; model_first_use_year left null.
safety.population: Postmenopausal women with advanced breast cancer, teprotumumab (R1507) plus letrozole
safety.reason: Regulator: monkeys did not predict hyperglycaemia
safety.judgement: Imported harm replaced by this disease's own patients (ruling). The monkey data were first public in the 2020 FDA review, after teprotumumab's own TED hyperglycaemia (2017), so a retrodiction that failed to reproduce it: contra. Cynomolgus IGF-1R is engaged, so the species could have shown it.

safety.model: MCF-7/AC-1 aromatase-expressing xenografts under letrozole (dalotuzumab, ridaforolimus)
safety.note: Ruling: Becker's 'all agents (both alone and in combination) were well tolerated' is a safety prediction. Patients on dalotuzumab plus ridaforolimus had unacceptable toxicity (stomatitis, hyperglycaemia), already public, so a failed retrodiction.
safety.quote: Lowering the ridaforolimus dose reduced the incidence of grade 3 stomatitis, but overall toxicity remained higher than acceptable at all doses without improved efficacy.
safety.confidence_note: Becker's tolerability statement rests on body weight, data not shown (low confidence). Dalotuzumab's own combination toxicity was public before Becker (SABCS 2013; Di Cosimo 2014 DLTs), so retrodiction true. Abstract-level for Baselga.
safety.population: ER+ advanced breast cancer previously treated with a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor
safety.judgement: Passing tolerability claim scored (ruling). Dose and safety retrodiction rests on the same drug's own earlier patient result, which exists here (dalotuzumab plus ridaforolimus), so contra with retrodiction true.
